proposals.evidence: Turner 6530 dēvátā explicitly cites European Romani devel 'God'. The source prints Zargari dévlā 'O God!' as a vocative stress example (p. 130 §2.5.2), and its noun morphology identifies the vocative -ā as probably Persian-derived (p. 130 §3.1.2). The Romani stem is assigned to Turner's family while the local vocative suffix and its contact history remain in the note. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.

proposals.evidence: Turner 434 ápara explicitly lists European Romani aver 'other'. The source prints Zargari āvur 'another; another one' in the indefinite-pronoun list (p. 136 §3.3.6.1). The vowel form is retained as printed; no immediate borrowing route is inferred. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.

proposals.evidence: The source prints the two-word Zargari phrase āvur dis 'the day after tomorrow' (p. 143 §3.20.1.2). Its lexical constituents are source āvur 'another' (newly linked to Turner 434) and dis 'day' (already linked to Turner 6333). This records two inherited components and preserves the idiomatic whole gloss; it does not posit an ancient whole-phrase etymon. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.
